item.title: One-shot is Enough: Boosting SAM for Medical Image Segmentation through Structured Information Modeling

In recent years, Foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization capabilities, but because they are primarily pre-trained on natural images, they perform poorly when faced with medical images. With sufficient labeled medical data, this challenge is somewhat alleviated. item.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
Segment Anything In-Context via Visual Demonstrations
item.description:
arXiv Query: search_query=all:"foundation model" AND all:medical AND all:segmen… · score 0.43

We present the Segment Anything Model via Visual Demonstrations (SAYD), a foundation model for in-context segmentation. Given visual demos comprising prompt images and their segmentation masks, SAYD segments coherent regions (e.g., objects or their parts) in a query image by establishing visual correspondences between the prompts and the query. SAYD generalizes to previously-unseen segmentation tasks, including those requiring tacit visual knowledge or involving concepts that are difficult to articulate unambiguously in language.
